1  [2024:RJ-JD:34455] (2 of 4) [CRLMB-10218/2024]
2. His first bail application was dismissed as not pressed by this Court vide order dated 01.04.2024 passed in SBCRLMB No.2474/2024.
Hence, the instant bail application.

3. It is contended on behalf of the accused-petitioner that the relations with victim were consensual thus, no case for the alleged offences is made out against him and his incarceration is not warranted.

There are no factors at play in the case at hand that may work against grant of bail to the accused-petitioner and he has been made an accused based on conjectures and surmises.
4.

Contrary to the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor opposes the bail application and submits that the present case is not fit for enlargement of accused on bail.

5. I have heard and considered the submissions made by both the parties and gone through the FIR,
the statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 & 164 of the Cr.P.C. as well as other material more particularly, the report under Section 173 Cr.P.C. perused the material available made available to this Court.
6. Perusal of the record revealing that the victim is a 27 years old grown up married lady.
She lodged the FIR on 12.05.2023 alleging therein that she was married with one Ganpat Lal and having two kids of 8 years and 4 years.
As per her narration, she came in contact with the petitioner a year ago from the lodging of the FIR.

She alleges that she was subjected to drink contaminated water as a result of which she felt unconscious and whereupon the petitioner took her nude photographs whereafter, she frequently used to talk with him and she takes a pretext that in the fear of [2024:RJ-JD:34455] (3 of 4) [CRLMB-10218/2024] disclosing the naked photographs, she submitted herself to the accused for sexual intercourse.

The investigation was initially conducted by one Madan Lal, Dy. S.P. and it is reflecting from the page 3 of the report under Section 173 Cr.P.C.
that several grounds have been mentioned therein on the basis of which a negative final report was proposed by saying that the complainant had levelled false allegation against the petitioner.

Under the direction of the superior officer, the investigation was further conducted by the Additional Superintendent of Police and whereupon he found the offence proved and then the petitioner was arrested and chargesheeted.

His first bail application was dismissed as not pressed by this Court vide order dated 01.04.2024 passed in SBCRLMB No.2474/2024 when the investigation was pending and no material particularly her statements under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C. and report under Section 173 Cr.P.C. was available on record.

After going through the overall material this Court feels that there is a force in the defence submission that a false case has been foisted against the petitioner and if any relationship exists between the petitioner and the victim, then the same were consensual; both the parties are married, therefore, no offence as alleged is made out if the case is seen from another aspect.

If this Court would make any observation regarding discrepancies Ashok @ Achlaram vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:34455) on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194081826/
2 appearing in the statements of the victim or any comment is made over the credibility and truthfulness of the allegation then the same may put a serious dent in the case of the prosecution and surely it will influence the [2024:RJ-JD:34455] (4 of 4) [CRLMB-10218/2024] trial, therefore,
desisting from doing so but feeling that it is fit case for grant of bail to the petitioner.

sentences.text: 7. It is nigh well settled law that at a pre-conviction stage; bail is a rule and denial from the same should be an exception.
The purpose behind keeping an accused behind the bars during trial would be to secure his presence on the day of conviction so that he may receive the sentence as would be awarded to him.
Otherwise, it is the rule of Crimnal Jurisprudence that he shall be presumed innocent until the guilt is proved.

8. Accordingly, the instant second bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner as named in the cause title shall be enlarged on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to do so.

(FARJAND ALI),J 98-Mamta/-
